supersedingProductRequirements.requirement: Sacred Art serves one canonical artwork registry across Calendar/Home, Mass Explorer/Formation, Rosary/Stations/Prayers, Historia Salutis/Atlas/genealogy/character stories, Saints, and selective Sacred Geography. Context links are typed, reciprocal and source backed.

Canonical identities are separate: ARTWORK_ID uniquely identifies the physical original; SUBJECT_ID identifies what is depicted; SCENE/EVENT_ID owns narrative passage; PERSON_ID owns actor; PLACE_ID owns map location; liturgical CALENDAR_ID identifies the observed day. Do not substitute another physical painting because artist/title match.

Lock user historical 0–5 artwork ratings and the 101 recorded editorial selections. An accepted artwork need not have five stars; artistic rating, contextual suitability, photograph fidelity and frame status are independent fields. Globally rejected scores 0–2 and excluded Fra Angelico/El Greco remain excluded.

Phone visual quality—not pixel dimensions or print-grade resolution—governs acquisition. Fit the entire painting on screen by default; no crop during acquisition. External frame removal is a separate reversible derivative and must not alter painted edges.

Authentic historical photographs and portraits are fully eligible for modern saints, preferably before generic imaginative portraits. Distinguish authentic likeness, lifetime photo, historic painted likeness, derivative portrait, commemorative image, illustration. Never create photorealistic 'originals' or falsely identify an icon as a painting.

Future traditional living sanctoral must use identity-safe saints mapping and distinguish 1962 feast from later supplementary dates. Not every modern canonized saint gets a separate mandatory image; feature priority saints and verify observed-day links independently.

For liturgical display: one suitable artwork for important Class I themes and major Sundays where feasible, using the actual 1962-oriented dynamic resolver and locally applicable overlays. Preference Gospel scene → appointed other Scripture → feast/mystery → actual saint → broader justified symbolism; 2026 date examples cannot hard-code future years.

Historia Salutis is Creation → New Creation with covenant/promise spine, Adam-to-Christ genealogy, 12 proposed narrative arcs, person stories, typology, and 151 existing canonical event IDs. One or a few excellent signature works per meaningful arc/story; no 151-event, 183-scene, 3,231-person, or 44-story mandatory image quota.

Preserve Matthew and Luke genealogical witnesses distinctly and keep biblical identity links evidence-based. Link relevant artwork to depicted people, passage, time/place/arc where established; no inferred relative, era or location.

Rosary retains 15 traditional mysteries as default; optional five Luminous mysteries are supplemental. OT–NT paired verses and Scripture typology do not create per-bead painting quotas. Reuse one strong iconographic anchor per mystery when available and exact scene matches for exceptional beads.

Mass Explorer owns 32 canonical Mass moments, with art as selective thematic, typological or historical annotation. Preserve LIVE/Simple/Missal reader and current card IDs; no imagery clutter, independent reader replacement, or mixing an explanatory painting with a photo of a liturgical object.

3D Living Glossary is a separate interactive Roman Catholic church/object experience. Photogrammetric church setting and sacred-vessel/vestment hotspot assets are not automatically counted as paintings. Link physical objects to relevant artworks only when documented.

Keep image-photo provenance, museum accession, checksum, depiction view/side, completeness, attribution certainty, original-source licence/photographer terms, and app commercial-use permission separate. Acquisition or CC0 label in one context does not automatically prove permission for other photos. Keep verified rights status distinct from source-photo count; existing 146/168 baseline was photographic, not a proven commercial-release total.

Do not repeat already acquired originals or research one painting at a time. Work in priority batches: existing approved/selected cross-module imagery, major calendar and Gospel anchors, significant narrative/character scenes, selective saints, lower priority context; no rating UI until acquisition inventory is ready.
